content: If you experience any of the following symptoms of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), seek emergency medical help immediately: painful red or purple skin that appears burned and peels off, flat red rashes or blisters on the skin, mouth, nose, or genitals, and red, painful, watery eyes. Omeprazole can also cause a severe allergic reaction known as DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms), which may affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. If you develop symptoms such as a skin rash, pale red bumps (hives), fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the feet, ankles, or legs, dark-colored urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), stop taking the medication and seek medical attention immediately. Omeprazole may also trigger or worsen lupus, an autoimmune disorder where the immune system attacks the body’s own cells and organs. Notify your healthcare provider if you experience new or worsening joint pain or a rash on your arms or cheeks. Long-term use of omeprazole (three years or more) can lead to vitamin B-12 deficiency, which may cause symptoms such as a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling and numbness in the hands or feet. If you experience these symptoms, stop taking the medication and consult your healthcare provider. Additionally, omeprazole can cause low magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia), which may result in seizures, abnormal heart rhythms, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. This risk is higher in individuals taking the medication long-term or in combination with other drugs that lower magnesium levels. If you notice any of these symptoms, discontinue use and contact your healthcare provider. Omeprazole may also increase the risk of bone loss and fractures, particularly in older adults or those taking high doses or using the medication for an extended period. Severe allergic reactions to omeprazole can occur, presenting as breathing difficulties, wheezing, a racing heart, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, itching, skin rash, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or fainting. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking the medication and seek immediate medical attention. People allergic to omeprazole, Prilosec, Prilosec OTC, other proton pump inhibitors, or any ingredients in the product should not use omeprazole. Always inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking to avoid potential drug interactions. Omeprazole should not be taken with certain medications, such as clopidogrel, cilostazol, citalopram, methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, certain antiretroviral drugs, St. John’s Wort, or rifampin, as these may interact with the medication. Omeprazole is used to treat conditions caused by excess stomach acid, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, erosive esophagitis, and Helicobacter pylori infections. It works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. The medication is available in various forms, including capsules, tablets, and powders for oral suspension. It should be stored at room temperature in a cool, dry place. Common side effects of omeprazole include headache, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, gas, and, in children, fever or respiratory infections. If you experience any bothersome side effects, contact your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, such as kidney problems, antibiotic-associated diarrhea, or severe skin reactions, require immediate medical attention. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, but do not double the dose. If you suspect an overdose, seek emergency medical help or contact a poison control center. Omeprazole should only be used as prescribed by a healthcare provider and is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn. It may take one to four days to take full effect. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult their healthcare provider before using omeprazole, as its effects on pregnancy and breast milk are not fully known.
